items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: He said, when I went to Baton Rouge, I met a fella up there called Green. He had Baton Rouge sewed up in clarinet. Man, that cat would play some clarinet. But after I was up there about six months, he was just another clarinet man.

ctx.x: What year did you start fooling with saxophone? Oh, around 29. 28, 29, somewhere. And how come you took up saxophone?

Well that was all that was playing around here at that time. I didn't give up clarinet. When I wanted to, one man I wanted to meet with clarinet was Sidney Bessier. Uh huh. But I never got a chance to play against Sidney because he was in New York. He left a week before I come here. I never got a chance to even hear him play, but on records that's all. But I sure wanted to play against Sidney. He said, when I went to Baton Rouge, I met a fella up there called Green. He had Baton Rouge sewed up in clarinet. Man,…

Who was that guy in Baton Rouge that didn't have any keys on his clarinet? Did you know him? No. That was strange. That's how he could play. Any number you wanted, but he just fingered the holes was all. Stopped everything else up, just used those three fingers on each hand.
